assumptions: The founder can use the family installer as a bounded design partner while remaining within the stated part-time limit, but that access does not imply an external customer pipeline.
No privileged CRO integration, exclusive channel relationship, proprietary dataset, or uniquely unmet product capability exists beyond the evidence provided.
Initial company pricing remains within the proposed 149-399 PLN monthly range, and operator revenue or European expansion is not treated as established.
The dated count of more than 14,000 enterprise certificates is a directional market indicator rather than a current count of active, reachable, paying firms.
AI can accelerate software and operational work, but regulatory interpretation, liability control, partner access, and technician behavior still require human expertise and validation.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Recurring regulated service events create a genuine job-completion control point from which evidence, asset history, and maintenance follow-up can be produced. The insight is useful but not distinctive: several Polish products already organize substantially the same compliance and field-service workflow, so the proposed service-revenue and speed wedge remains a hypothesis rather than a newly identified market gap.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Equipment-level records, changing refrigerant rules, recurring visits, and inspections create persistent administrative and error-avoidance pain. Published paid competitor tiers provide indirect evidence that some firms pay for workflow software, but a free direct substitute and official registry access limit willingness to pay for compliance alone; willingness to switch or pay for the incremental speed and repeat-service promise is unknown rather than disproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Subscription SaaS can in principle deliver recurring revenue and high gross margin, and the pilot fits the stated capital envelope. However, low Polish price anchors leave little room for channel commission, onboarding, support, and contracted regulatory review; CAC, churn, support load, cash payback, and actual gross margin are unresolved. The illustrative founder-wealth path relies on roughly 2,000 firms plus operator accounts, an aggressive share before any repeatable acquisition or retention evidence.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small certified Polish HVAC, refrigeration, and heat-pump firms are a coherent beachhead with a common recurring workflow and a regulator-reported universe large enough for a focused software business. The available firm count is dated and not segmented by activity or reachability, while achieving the stated wealth outcome domestically would require a substantial share of this already-served niche or success in an unvalidated operator or foreign segment.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Montak directly overlaps the proposed protocols, equipment history, and recurring inspections at free and low paid tiers, while Montero, Fieldworker, and Clima Pro add further substitutes. CRO and UDT retain the authoritative rails, and the candidate has no demonstrated exclusive integration, channel, or workflow advantage; competent execution could win customers, but a dominant position is not presently supported.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven equipment-and-service graph could extend to multi-site operators, additional refrigerants, maintenance contracts, adjacent field-service workflows, and other EU markets. Those adjacencies are logically connected, but regulatory localization, incumbent competition, channel acquisition, and the lack of operator demand evidence mean expansion cannot yet carry the economics of the beachhead.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accumulated equipment histories, recurring schedules, and embedded job routines can create modest switching costs and retention. The underlying regulatory logic is public, customer data is permissioned rather than uniquely owned, incumbents can add similar automation, and no exclusive distribution or data right is evidenced, so the advantage is likely to be copied unless the business secures a stronger control point.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Faster technician entry and recovered repeat-service revenue could be behavior-changing if they are large and measurable. No evidence yet shows a material speed, revenue, accuracy, convenience, or price advantage over existing Polish products, and the proposed feature set substantially overlaps them; the claimed benefit is therefore plausible but not yet strong enough to motivate switching.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Recent EU rules, broader certification scope, changing CRO fields, and a meaningful inspection program create a timely need to maintain structured records across refrigerant transitions. This is a real tailwind, although the visible competitor set shows that the market has already recognized it and regulatory change also raises ongoing product-maintenance cost.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer provides unusually good access for workflow observation and one credible pilot without founder-brand exposure. It does not solve scalable acquisition: wholesalers, distributors, and trainers have made no commitment, their economics are unknown, and fragmented small firms at low ARPU can be costly to sell and onboard. Technician-to-customer reminders may aid retention or downstream revenue but are not yet a proven customer-acquisition loop.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A narrow mobile prototype and single-company pilot are technically feasible within the founder's data/automation strengths, time, and capital, especially with AI leverage. Reliable regulatory logic, any CRO transfer method, field usability, security, support liability, and productized onboarding remain material requirements; scaling beyond early firms would require delegated regulatory expertise and operations rather than founder-led consulting.

main_structural_strength: A mandatory, recurring technician job-completion event can anchor asset history, customer proof, and maintenance renewal in one workflow, and the founder has unusually low-cost access to a real installer for tightly measured design-partner testing.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed product lacks a demonstrated behavior-changing advantage or protected distribution control point against multiple direct Polish substitutes, including a free tier, which in turn caps pricing power and makes the customer share required for the wealth path difficult to acquire economically.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Montak already offers the central proposed bundle—HVAC protocols, F-gas reminders, equipment history, and recurring inspections—with a non-expiring free tier and paid plans at 199 and 399 PLN per month, while three additional Polish products overlap the same workflow.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A multi-firm paid pilot should show a material reduction in technician minutes per job or incremental maintenance revenue versus the best incumbent, conversion at sustainable pricing, low-touch onboarding and support, six-to-twelve-month retention, an accurate CRO transfer workflow, and a committed channel with measured CAC and payback.
highest_value_structural_change: Shift from standalone compliance SaaS to a distributor-embedded job-close-to-renewal operating layer: prefill equipment and parts data from distributor transactions, automate maintenance-contract capture and parts reorder, treat compliance output as table stakes, and proceed only after securing committed channel distribution and data access that incumbents cannot readily replicate.
